decisive_items: the anti-acetylcholine receptor antibody and the edrophonium tests were negative
response.rationale: R3 best fits the fluctuating ptosis and diplopia with normal pupils and full extraocular movements; negative AChR antibody and edrophonium testing do not exclude seronegative ocular myasthenia gravis. R1 only captures the traumatic/orthostatic headache component and lacks a specific ocular syndrome. R2 and R4 are contradicted by the normal pupillary light reflexes and absence of extraocular movement limitation, and R5 is contradicted by normal pupils.

rejected.why: Superior orbital fissure syndrome would require ophthalmoplegia and often pupillary/sensory changes; normal pupillary reflexes and no EOM limitation disconfirm.
Third cranial nerve palsy would cause limitation of extraocular movements and commonly pupillary involvement; both are absent.
Adie syndrome requires a tonic pupil; the pupillary light reflexes are explicitly normal.
